question: How does PRINCE2 7 define a project?
options: A temporary organization that is to deliver one or more business products according to an agreed business case
A set of recurring activities by which an organization operates and maintains its products and services over the long term
A permanent organizational structure that coordinates a group of related changes to achieve strategic objectives
A sequence of planned activities managed by a project manager within a budget approved by company management
explanation: PRINCE2 sees a project as a temporary organization that is created to deliver one or more business products in line with an agreed business case. Recurring activities represent normal operations (business as usual), and a permanent structure coordinating related changes does not match the temporary nature of a project. A mere sequence of activities led by the PM overlooks what is essential – the temporary organization and the link to the business case.

question:
Which two of the following items are among the five integrated elements of PRINCE2 7?
1. Themes
2. People
3. Project environment
4. Project context
options: 2 and 4
1 and 3
1 and 2
3 and 4
explanation: PRINCE2 7 rests on five integrated elements: principles, people, practices, processes and project context. Themes and project environment are terms from the 6th edition – themes were replaced by practices, and instead of the project environment we now speak of the project context.

image.alt: Diagram of the five integrated elements of PRINCE2 7: principles, people, practices and processes inside the project context frame.

question: What organizational arrangement of a project does PRINCE2 7 assume?
options: None in particular; however, there are always users, suppliers and those who decide on the investment
A relationship between a customer and an external supplier governed by a contract for the delivery of finished products
A project as part of a programme that provides it with the business case and the project mandate
A project within a single organization in which all team members are its employees
explanation: PRINCE2 does not start from any particular arrangement: a project can be standalone or part of a programme or portfolio, and suppliers can be internal or external. In every project, however, there are users, suppliers and those who decide on the investment – hence the three interests of business, user and supplier. Commercial relationships with external suppliers are then addressed by the commercial management approach.

question: Fill in the missing word: PRINCE2 7 manages project performance in seven areas (performance targets) – benefits, costs, time, quality, scope, risk and ______.
options: sustainability
communication
stakeholder engagement
compliance
explanation: The seven performance targets of PRINCE2 7 are benefits, costs, time, quality, scope, risk and, new, sustainability; a tolerance can be set for each of them. The 6th edition worked with only six areas, without sustainability. Communication, stakeholders and compliance are not separate performance targets.

image.alt: Two columns: the seven practices of PRINCE2 7 and the seven performance targets, including sustainability.

question: Which characteristic of a project expresses that a project brings more threats and opportunities than normal operations (business as usual)?
options: Uncertainty
Unique
Cross-functional
Temporary
explanation: The change that a project delivers carries more threats and opportunities than normal operations – PRINCE2 calls this property uncertainty. Being unique means that each project differs from the others in some way; it does increase uncertainty, but it is not what denotes it. Being temporary and involving people from across units describe other properties of a project.

question:
Which two of the following properties are among the characteristics by which a project differs from normal operations?
1. Temporary
2. Cross-functional
3. Repetitive
4. Predictable
options: 1 and 2
3 and 4
1 and 3
2 and 4
explanation: PRINCE2 lists five characteristics of a project: change, temporary, cross-functional, unique and uncertainty. Repeatability and predictability, on the contrary, are typical of normal operations – a project is unique and carries higher uncertainty.

question: Which delivery methods does PRINCE2 7 explicitly distinguish?
options: Linear-sequential, iterative-incremental and hybrid
Plan-driven, change-driven and hybrid
Waterfall, iterative-incremental and continuous delivery
Linear-sequential, parallel-concurrent and iterative
explanation: PRINCE2 7 describes three delivery methods: linear-sequential, iterative-incremental and a hybrid combination of the two. A project can use more than one of them, and management according to PRINCE2 works with any of them. The other triples mix terms from other frameworks or categories that PRINCE2 does not use.

question: Fill in the missing word: With the ______ delivery method, the solution is created in repeated cycles, each cycle adds another functional part and the requirements are continuously refined.
options: iterative-incremental
linear-sequential
predictive
waterfall
explanation: The iterative-incremental delivery method delivers the solution in repeated cycles in increments and the requirements are refined as it proceeds – typically these are agile ways of working. The linear-sequential (waterfall, predictive) approach, on the contrary, proceeds in consecutive steps and the products are largely specified in advance.

question: How does PRINCE2 7 describe a portfolio, within which a project may take place?
options: As an organization’s total investment in the change needed to achieve its strategic objectives
As a temporary structure that coordinates related projects and work in order to achieve benefits
As the directing level that commissions the project, appoints the executive and sets its tolerances
As the set of all products that the project hands over into normal operations, including documentation
explanation: A portfolio represents an organization’s total investment in the change by which it wants to achieve its strategic objectives. A temporary structure coordinating related projects and work in order to achieve benefits is a programme, and the directing level of a project is the business layer. A project can be part of a programme or portfolio, but can also be standalone.

question: Which statement about the PRINCE2 7 method is correct?
options: It is universal – it can be applied to a project of any scale and in any sector, together with specialist ways of working
It contains specialist techniques for specialised work, for example for the design and development of software or buildings
It is suited mainly to linear projects; for iterative delivery it has to be replaced by another project management method
It prescribes a uniform form of all management products that the project may not tailor in any way
explanation: One of the main properties of PRINCE2 is universality: the method can be applied to any project regardless of scale, type or sector, and it works alongside specialist models. PRINCE2 does not itself address the specialist work, it is compatible with all delivery methods including iterative-incremental, and management products are tailored to the project.

question: What applies to the application of the seven PRINCE2 7 principles in a project?
options: All of them must be applied; only the way in which they are fulfilled in the project is tailored
Those that the project board selects at initiation as relevant for the project are applied
For small projects the principles of business case, stages and exceptions are enough, the others are optional
They are good-practice recommendations that can be replaced by own rules during tailoring
explanation: The principles are guiding obligations: a project that does not apply all seven is not a PRINCE2 project. What can be tailored is how the principles are fulfilled, not omitting them. Selection of principles by the board or their replacement with own rules would negate the very essence of the method.

image.alt: Overview of the seven PRINCE2 7 principles with their names and a short explanation.

question: What applies in PRINCE2 7 to the so-called minimum requirements for the individual practices?
options: They are not set; the method relies on the application of the principles and on agreed tolerances
Each practice has a fixed minimum that cannot be omitted or adjusted in any way during tailoring
They are set only for the Business case and Progress practices, the others do not have them
They are determined by the business layer for each project separately and the board records them in the PID
explanation: The 6th edition defined minimum requirements for each theme. PRINCE2 7 abolished them – the method rests on observing the seven principles and on tolerances agreed between the levels of management. The option with a fixed minimum for each practice thus describes the state from the previous edition.

question: What does the principle Ensure continued business justification require?
options: That there is a valid reason to start the project and that this reason lasts throughout the project
That the business case is formally approved by the business layer before each stage and before the closure of the project
That the project delivers all the benefits stated in the business case before its closure
That the business case is approved once and for all at initiation and does not change in later stages
explanation: The principle requires that a justification exist for starting the project and that it remain valid throughout; if it lapses, the project should be changed or stopped. The business case is therefore continually updated and the project board checks it at decision points. Most benefits, moreover, materialise only after the project ends, so they cannot be required before its closure.

image.alt: Overview of the seven PRINCE2 7 principles with their names and a short explanation.

question: Fill in the missing word: One of the PRINCE2 7 principles reads “Define roles, responsibilities and ______”.
options: relationships
reporting lines
accountabilities
authorities
explanation: In the 7th edition the principle was extended to Define roles, responsibilities and relationships: in addition to agreed roles and responsibilities that engage the business, user and supplier interests, it stresses building relationships with internal and external stakeholders and among them. In the 6th edition the principle was called Defined roles and responsibilities.

image.alt: Overview of the seven PRINCE2 7 principles with their names and a short explanation.

question:
Which two of the following statements about the principle Learn from experience are true?
1. Lessons are recorded only at project closure in the lessons report.
2. Lessons are the sole responsibility of project support, which keeps the lessons log.
3. Lessons from earlier projects are sought already at the start of the project.
4. Seeking lessons is the responsibility of everyone who takes part in the project.
options: 3 and 4
1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
explanation: Lessons are sought at the start (from earlier projects), recorded and applied throughout the whole project and handed over to the organization at closure; everyone involved should seek them. The lessons log is therefore kept throughout the project, not only at closure, and project support can at most administer it.

image.alt: Overview of the seven PRINCE2 7 principles with their names and a short explanation.

question: Which of the following steps is a permissible tailoring of PRINCE2 7?
options: Merge the highlight report with a regular monthly report that the organization already uses
Omit the principle Manage by stages, because the project is to last only four months and is simple
Assign the executive role to the project manager to speed up decision-making
Set no tolerances and instead escalate every deviation, however small, to the board
explanation: Tailoring may combine or simplify management products, align terminology and the form of reporting with the organization’s habits, or adjust the degree of formality. What cannot be done is omit a principle (a project must have at least two stages), combine the executive role with the project manager role, or give up the tolerances on which management by exception rests.

question: What is the minimum number of management stages a project must have according to the principle Manage by stages?
options: Two – the initiation stage and at least one further stage
Two – Starting up a project and one delivery stage
Three – the initiation, delivery and closing stages
One – for small projects a single stage is enough
explanation: A PRINCE2 project has at least two management stages: the initiation stage and at least one further (delivery) stage. Starting up a project takes place before the project (pre-project) and is not a stage. Closing a project takes place at the end of the last stage, not as a separate stage.

image.alt: Overview of the seven PRINCE2 7 principles with their names and a short explanation.

question: What is the main benefit of dividing a project into management stages according to the principle Manage by stages?
options: Stage boundaries serve the board as decision points on whether and how to continue with the project
Each stage corresponds to one specialist phase of work, for example analysis, development or testing
The project board can limit itself to checking the project only at its initiation and closure
The whole project can be planned in detail down to the level of individual tasks right at initiation
explanation: Managing by stages gives the project board a decision point at each stage boundary: it assesses the results achieved and the validity of the business case and decides whether to approve the next stage. Detailed planning is done only within the planning horizon, that is, stage by stage. Management stages need not correspond to specialist (technical) phases of work.

question: Fill in the missing word: The principle Manage by exception defines the delegated authority of each level of management by means of ______ set for the individual performance targets.
options: tolerances
change budgets
acceptance criteria
control milestones
explanation: Manage by exception sets tolerances, that is, permitted deviations, for the performance targets (time, costs, quality, scope, benefits, risk and sustainability) at each level of management. As long as a deviation stays within tolerance, the lower level handles it itself; the higher level intervenes only when a breach of tolerance is forecast (an exception). A change budget and acceptance criteria are different tools.

image.alt: The chain of business layer, Project Board, Project manager and Team manager: tolerances are set from the top down and exceptions are escalated from the bottom up.

question: An insurance company stops a new product project because, after a change in regulation, the product would no longer bring the expected benefits. Which principle is applied by this?
options: Ensure continued business justification
Define roles, responsibilities and relationships
Focus on products
Learn from experience
explanation: According to the principle Ensure continued business justification, the justification of the project must last throughout; when it lapses (here because of the change in regulation), the project should be changed or stopped. The other principles concern roles and relationships, products and lessons, not the duration of the reason for the investment.

image.alt: Overview of the seven PRINCE2 7 principles with their names and a short explanation.

question: While preparing the project, the project manager of an e-shop requests the final reports of two similar earlier projects and takes their recommendations into account in the project approach. Which principle is she applying?
options: Learn from experience
Focus on products
Manage by exception
Define roles, responsibilities and relationships
explanation: Seeking and using lessons from earlier projects right at the start is a typical manifestation of the principle Learn from experience (in the process Starting up a project this is the activity Assess previous lessons). Lessons are then recorded in the lessons log and applied throughout the project. The other principles concern products, tolerances and roles.

image.alt: Overview of the seven PRINCE2 7 principles with their names and a short explanation.

question: Which statement best captures the principle Focus on products?
options: The project defines and delivers products with a special emphasis on users’ requirements and expectations regarding quality
The project delivers products as quickly as possible, and therefore their descriptions are created only after the products are completed and handed over
The project concentrates mainly on managing activities; products are only a by-product of well-managed work
The project tries to deliver as many products as possible within the approved budget regardless of their use
explanation: Focus on products means that the project first clearly defines the products – their purpose, composition and quality requirements in product descriptions – and these then drive planning, quality control and acceptance. Planning therefore starts from products, not from activities, and product descriptions are created before the products are made, not after.

image.alt: Overview of the seven PRINCE2 7 principles with their names and a short explanation.

question: Why, according to the principle Manage by stages, is only the nearest stage always planned in detail?
options: Precise planning is possible only within the planning horizon, which is limited in time
The stage plan replaces the project plan, which is no longer maintained after initiation
The project plan is created only in the last stage, when all the products are known
A detailed plan of the whole project would violate the principle Manage by exception
explanation: With sufficient accuracy one can plan only a limited time ahead (the planning horizon). PRINCE2 therefore combines a high-level project plan, created already at initiation and updated at stage boundaries, with a detailed plan of the nearest stage. The stage plan thus does not replace the project plan but supplements it.

question:
Which two of the following items are among the factors according to which PRINCE2 7 is tailored to a project?
1. The executive’s personal preferences
2. The delivery method used
3. The capability of the project team
4. The number of principles that the board wants to apply
options: 2 and 3
1 and 4
1 and 2
3 and 4
explanation: The principle Tailor to suit the project adapts the method to the size, complexity, importance and riskiness of the project, its environment, the delivery method used and the capability of the team. An individual’s personal preferences are not an objective factor, and the number of principles applied is not chosen – all seven always apply.

question: The project manager of a small internal project proposes to omit the Risk practice altogether because he considers the project simple. What applies according to PRINCE2 7?
options: The practice can be simplified and adapted, but its purpose must remain fulfilled
The practice can be omitted if the project board explicitly approves it at initiation and records it in the PID
The practice can be omitted because practices, unlike principles, are only recommended
The practice cannot be adjusted in any way; only processes, roles and management products can be tailored
explanation: Tailoring means adapting practices to the context – for example simplifying the procedure or combining documents – not omitting them; the purpose of the practice must remain fulfilled. Not even the board’s consent makes the Risk practice an optional part. At the same time, it is not true that practices cannot be adjusted – they are tailored just like processes.

question: In which management product is it documented how the PRINCE2 method will be tailored in the project?
options: In the project initiation documentation (PID)
In the project mandate from the business layer
In the lessons log as part of the project log
In the end stage report of the first stage
explanation: Tailoring requirements are agreed during initiation (the activity Agree tailoring requirements in the process Initiating a project) and documented in the PID, which is approved by the project board. The project mandate comes from the business layer before the project starts, and the lessons log serves to record lessons, not decisions on tailoring the method.

image.alt: Two containers: the PID with nine management approaches and the project log with six records from the daily log to the product register.

question: Who approves the tailoring of the method that is captured in the PID?
options: The project board when authorizing the project
The project manager, who assembles the PID
Project assurance after reviewing the whole PID
The business layer when issuing the mandate
explanation: The tailoring of the method is captured in the PID and the project board approves it when authorizing the project – thereby it also approves the proposed tailoring. The project manager assembles the PID but does not approve it themselves; project assurance can assess the suitability of the tailoring and advise the board. The business layer can limit tailoring through its standards, but it does not decide on the PID.

question: What does the term organizational ecosystem denote in PRINCE2 7?
options: The internal parts of an organization and its external relationships, for example with customers, partners, suppliers or regulators
The parts of the business, users and suppliers who take part in a particular project or are affected by it
The structure of the roles of the project management team, including links to the business layer and to external suppliers
The set of information systems, data and tools that the organization uses in managing its projects
explanation: The organizational ecosystem includes the internal parts of an organization (employees, governance, owners) and its external relationships – customers, partners, suppliers, regulators or competitors. The parts of the business, users and suppliers involved in a particular project or affected by it make up the project ecosystem. The structure of roles is the project management team structure.

question: Fill in the missing word: The parts of the business, users and suppliers who take part in the project or are affected by it make up the ______.
options: project ecosystem
project team
project management team
organizational ecosystem
explanation: The project ecosystem consists of all the parts of the business, users and suppliers who are involved in the project or are affected by it. The project team and the project management team include only those who work on or manage the project, not the affected parties. The organizational ecosystem is broader – it includes the whole organization and its external relationships.

question: What is the relationship between the project ecosystem and organizational ecosystems?
options: The project ecosystem lies within one or more organizational ecosystems and overlaps with them
The organizational ecosystem is part of the project ecosystem and the project manages it for the duration of the project
The two ecosystems are separate and are linked only by the executive as the representative of the business layer
They are synonyms that PRINCE2 7 distinguishes only by whether the supplier is internal or external
explanation: A project arises within an organization (or several organizations, for example the customer and suppliers), so its ecosystem lies within the organizational ecosystems and overlaps with them. The project does not manage the whole organization, and the two ecosystems are neither separate nor identical; the relationships at their interface, on the contrary, need to be actively managed.

question: Residents of a housing estate mistakenly believe that a new logistics centre will increase noise in their neighbourhood and organise a petition. Are they stakeholders of the project according to PRINCE2 7?
options: Yes, anyone who merely perceives that the project will affect them is also a stakeholder
No, mere assumptions about the impact are not enough, because the project will in fact not affect them
No, a stakeholder is only someone who has a formal role or contract in the project
Yes, but only if they are formally represented in the project board by the senior user
explanation: A stakeholder is any person, group or organization that can affect the project, can be affected by it, or believes it will be affected by it. The residents are therefore stakeholders and the project should communicate with them, even though their concern is not justified. A formal role in the project or representation on the board is not a condition.

question: What does the term change management mean in PRINCE2 7?
options: The way in which an organization moves from its current state to the required target state
The management of requests for change of products included in the project baseline
The procedure by which the change authority approves changes within the change budget
The updating of the business case and plans at a stage boundary according to changes in the project environment
explanation: In PRINCE2 7, change management concerns organizational change – how the organization and its people move from the current state to the target state and embrace the new situation. The management of requests for change to the baseline (change control), including decisions by the change authority, belongs to the Issues practice. Confusing these two terms is a common mistake.

question:
Which two of the following components of the PID belong to the People element?
1. Change management approach
2. Issue management approach
3. Commercial management approach
4. Communication management approach
options: 1 and 4
2 and 3
1 and 2
3 and 4
explanation: The PID: change management approach (how the project will support organizational change) and the PID: communication management approach (communication with the project ecosystem) belong to the People element. The issue management approach belongs to the Issues practice and the commercial management approach to the Organizing practice.

question: What applies according to PRINCE2 7 to the culture of a project?
options: It should be aligned with the culture of the organizational ecosystem in which the project operates
The project should create its own culture independent of the organizations involved
The culture of the project is determined by the supplier, because its people do most of the work
There is only one culture in the whole organization, which the project adopts unchanged
explanation: Culture consists of shared values, attitudes, objectives and ways of working. Different parts of an organization, as well as different organizations, can have different cultures, and the project must therefore align its culture with its organizational ecosystem – it should neither replace it with its own culture nor adopt only the supplier’s culture.

question: Fill in the missing word: ______ is a set of shared values, attitudes, objectives and ways of working that characterize an organization or part of it.
options: Culture
Leadership
Governance
Ecosystem
explanation: PRINCE2 7 describes culture as the shared values, attitudes, objectives and ways of working of a group of people; more than one can exist within a single organization. Leadership is influencing and motivating people, governance is the framework of management and decision-making, and an ecosystem denotes the parts of an organization or project and their relationships.

question: What does co-creation mean in PRINCE2 7?
options: Involving users and other key people in the design of products and ways of working
Joint funding of the project by several organizations on the basis of a shared business case
Dividing the work among several suppliers, each of whom delivers its own part of the product
Joint approval of management products by the executive, senior user and senior supplier
explanation: Co-creation means that users and other key influencers take an active part in shaping the products and in how the work will be done. As a result, they find it easier to take the change on as their own. It is not about joint funding, dividing the delivery among suppliers, or an approval mechanism of the project board.

question: Which statement correctly distinguishes leadership and management?
options: Leadership motivates and influences people to achieve objectives; management directs the performance of tasks according to agreed procedures
Management motivates and influences people to achieve objectives; leadership directs the performance of tasks according to agreed procedures
Leadership is reserved for the project board, whereas management is performed by the project manager and team managers
Leadership is needed only for iterative delivery, whereas management is needed for linear-sequential delivery
explanation: Leadership is about motivating and influencing people so that they achieve objectives together (influence, collaboration, feedback); management is about directing the performance of tasks according to agreed ways of working. All levels of management and all delivery methods need both – it is neither a privilege of the board nor a matter for one type of project.

question: Why does PRINCE2 7 favour leadership based on influence and collaboration over a "command and control" approach in project teams?
options: Teams are temporary and often span several organisations, so the leader's formal authority is limited
The method forbids team members from being subordinate to the project manager or team manager
Directive management may be exercised only by the project board, which alone has formal authority
Collaboration reduces project costs and is therefore a mandatory part of every business case
explanation: Project teams are temporary and bring together people from different departments and organisations, so the project manager or team manager has weaker formal authority over them than a line manager would. This is why PRINCE2 7 stresses leadership built on influence, collaboration and frequent feedback. The other options state rules that the method does not lay down.

question: Whom does the People element in PRINCE2 7 include?
options: The people who work on the project as well as the people affected by the change the project delivers
Only the members of the project management team, i.e. the board, PM, team managers and project support
The project's HR agenda, i.e. recruitment, remuneration and performance appraisal of team members
Stakeholders outside the project; the people who work on the project are covered by the Organizing practice
explanation: The People element concerns the people who work on the project and their relationships with one another, but also the people affected by the delivered change, for example users in day-to-day operations. Limiting it to the project management team would overlook those whose acceptance of the change the benefits depend on, and conversely, leaving out the project team would ignore team leadership and collaboration, which the People element addresses. The HR agenda (recruitment, remuneration) is not part of its scope.

question: Why is organisational change management important for a PRINCE2 7 project?
options: Benefits arise only when the people affected by the project accept the change and start using it
Without it, requests for change and off-specifications cannot be recorded or assessed in the project
It is the only way to keep the project within the tolerances for time, cost and scope
It replaces communication with stakeholders, which then no longer needs to be planned separately
explanation: Projects deliver change that affects day-to-day operations. Outputs alone do not bring benefits – benefits arise only when people accept the new situation and actually use the change; that is why organisational change management is key. Handling requests for change and off-specifications belongs to the Issues practice (change control).

question: During stakeholder analysis, the project manager finds that a warehouse shift supervisor has no formal role in the project, but colleagues value his opinion greatly. How should the project proceed according to PRINCE2 7?
options: Actively engage him, because even people without a formal role can significantly influence acceptance of the change
Not engage him, because stakeholder engagement applies only to holders of formal roles
Propose that the executive appoint him to the project board as a senior user because of his influence
Communicate with him only when the products are handed over into operations, when the change actually affects him
explanation: PRINCE2 7 stresses that, besides holders of formal roles, it is necessary to actively engage key people without a formal role who influence the project or are affected by it – for example informal opinion leaders among the users. The shift supervisor does not have to become a board member because of this – the senior user role carries responsibility for user requirements and benefits, it is not a way to involve influential people – and postponing his involvement until the products are handed over would jeopardise acceptance of the change.

question: What does the PID: communication management approach define?
options: The means and frequency of communication with the project ecosystem and the way feedback is obtained
One-way dissemination of project information so as to limit stakeholders' questions and comments
The format and frequency of highlight reports through which the project manager communicates exclusively with the board
The way requests to change the project baseline are recorded and evaluated
explanation: The communication management approach describes the means by which, and how often, the project will communicate with its ecosystem and how it will obtain feedback – it is a managed two-way flow of information. One-way "broadcasting" is a typical misconception. Highlight reports are just one form of communication, and changes to the baseline are handled by the issue management approach.

question:
Which two of the following statements about communication in PRINCE2 7 are true?
1. Communication should be two-way and include feedback from stakeholders.
2. The way of communicating is adapted to whether the team works on site, remotely or in a hybrid way.
3. Informal communication in the project has no value and should not be given attention.
4. Only the executive may communicate with external stakeholders.
options: 1 and 2
3 and 4
1 and 3
2 and 4
explanation: Communication in PRINCE2 7 is a managed two-way flow of information with feedback, and it is adapted to whether the team works together on site, remotely or in a hybrid way. Informal communication matters too, and various roles communicate with external stakeholders according to the communication management approach, not only the executive.

question: How do capability and competence differ in effective teams in PRINCE2 7?
options: Capability expresses what the team as a whole can do; competence is the skills of individual members
Competence expresses what the team as a whole can do; capability is the skills of individual members
Capability is the certification achieved by team members; competence is their practical experience in the field
Capability is assessed by the senior supplier at the supplier; competence is assessed by the PM for internal people
explanation: Team capability describes what the team as a whole is able to achieve, whereas competence concerns the skills of individuals. Together with diversity, these are characteristics of an effective team, and any gaps identified are addressed, for example, through training or by adding to the team. Beware: in the Business case practice, capability means something different – a complete set of outputs.

question: The project manager finds that the team lacks competence in cybersecurity, which the project needs. How should he proceed according to PRINCE2 7?
options: Address the gap, for example by training existing members or by adding an expert to the team
Record it as an off-specification, because the products will not meet the quality specification
Immediately submit an exception report to the board, because the project tolerance has been exceeded
Lower the acceptance criteria so that they match the current skills of the team members
explanation: PRINCE2 7 expects gaps in team capability and competence to be actively addressed – through training or recruitment, i.e. by adding to the team. An off-specification concerns a product that fails to meet its specification, not the skills of the team, and an exception report comes into consideration only when a tolerance breach is forecast. Lowering the acceptance criteria would only mask the problem.

question: The project team consists of people from three suppliers who work mostly remotely and barely know one another. What does PRINCE2 7 emphasise in such a situation?
options: Deliberately building trust and team cohesion even in a virtual or hybrid environment
Dividing the work so that people from different suppliers do not have to collaborate at all
Replacing team meetings with written checkpoint reports from individual team members
Transferring responsibility for leading the team to the senior supplier, because these are external people
explanation: Effective teams need trust and social cohesion; in virtual and hybrid teams these must be built deliberately – through joint activities, ways-of-working rules and regular interaction. Separating people, replacing communication with written reports, or moving team leadership away from the PM and team managers would, on the contrary, weaken cohesion.

question: How is the People element reflected in the other elements of PRINCE2 7?
options: Human aspects appear in all the principles, practices and processes
People is the eighth practice, which complements the Organizing and Progress practices
It concerns only the Starting up a project process, in which the team is appointed
It replaces the Organizing practice, which was abolished in PRINCE2 7
explanation: PRINCE2 7 puts people at the centre of the method: human aspects are reflected in all the principles (e.g. relationships), practices (roles, communication in reporting, stakeholder input into requirements, risk culture) and processes (appointing the team, agreeing approaches, handing over and accepting products). People is not a practice, and the Organizing practice still exists in the 7th edition.

question: Fill in the missing word: How the project will support the organisation and its people in moving to a new way of working is described by the PID: ______ management approach.
options: change
issue
benefits
communication
explanation: The change management approach describes how the project will support organisational change, i.e. the transition of the organisation and its people from the current state to the target state. The issue management approach deals with issues and control of changes to the baseline (change control), the benefits management approach with measuring benefits, and the communication management approach with communication with the project ecosystem.

image.alt: Two containers: the PID with nine management approaches and the project log with six records, from the daily log to the product register.

question:
Which two of the following characteristics does PRINCE2 7 give as marks of an effective team?
1. Uniformity
2. Seniority
3. Diversity
4. Competence
options: 3 and 4
1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
explanation: PRINCE2 7 associates effective teams with diversity, the capability of the team as a whole and the competence of individuals. Neither the uniformity of members nor their seniority is in itself a mark of an effective team – on the contrary, diverse experience and perspectives are an advantage.

question: What does the term collaboration express in PRINCE2 7?
options: People working together across the project and organisational ecosystem towards shared goals
A contractually regulated relationship between the customer and an external supplier according to the commercial approach
Sharing the impact of a risk with a partner so that they share any losses and gains of the project
Delegating authority between the levels of project management through defined tolerances
explanation: Collaboration means that people from different parts of the project and organisational ecosystem actively work together on shared goals; closely related is co-creation, where users help shape products and ways of working. Contractual relationships are addressed by the commercial management approach, risk sharing is a risk response (share), and delegation through tolerances corresponds to the Manage by exception principle.

question: Where, according to PRINCE2 7, are the key stakeholders of a project often found?
options: At the interface between the project ecosystem and the organisational ecosystem
Exclusively within the project management team, most often on the board
Mostly outside the organisation, for example among regulators and competitors
At the delivering level, because that is where the project's products are created
explanation: The project ecosystem lies within organisational ecosystems and overlaps with them; key stakeholders are often found precisely at their interface – for example heads of operational units who will take over the change. That is why relationships at this boundary need to be actively managed. Stakeholders are not limited to the project management team, nor are they found mostly outside the organisation.

question: Which of the following areas is NOT part of the People chapter in PRINCE2 7?
options: Change control (managing changes to the baseline)
Leading successful change
Leading successful teams
Communication
explanation: The People chapter deals with leading successful change, leading successful teams, communication, and the fact that people stand at the centre of the method. Change control, i.e. managing changes to the baseline, belongs to the Issues practice – it must not be confused with organisational change management.

question: Why does PRINCE2 7 emphasise cultural intelligence in project teams?
options: Teams often bring together people from different organisations, professions and countries with differing cultures
The project is supposed to impose a single culture on the team and gradually eliminate the members' differences
It is a criterion by which the senior supplier selects team members on the supplier side
Cultural intelligence is one of the seven performance targets that the board monitors
explanation: Project teams tend to be temporary and made up of people from different organisations, fields and countries who bring different cultures with them. Cultural intelligence helps to understand these differences and work with them effectively rather than suppress them. It is not one of the seven performance targets (benefits, costs, time, quality, scope, sustainability, risk).

question: What is the main purpose of the project initiation documentation (PID)?
options: To summarise the information from initiation on which the board authorises the project and which forms its baseline
To provide the information on which the board decides whether to start the project at all by initiating it
To continuously record issues, risks, lessons and product status throughout the duration of the project
To formally hand over to the business layer an evaluation of the project's results and recommendations for follow-on steps
explanation: The PID is a summary of the products created or updated during initiation; it is used to obtain authorisation of the project and then serves as a baseline that is reviewed at each stage boundary. The basis for the decision to start initiation is the project brief, ongoing records belong in the project log, and the evaluation of the project at the end is contained in the end project report.

image.alt: Two containers: the PID with nine management approaches and the project log with six records, from the daily log to the product register.

question:
Which two of the following items are part of the project log in PRINCE2 7?
1. Business case
2. Product register
3. Daily log
4. Work package description
options: 2 and 3
1 and 4
1 and 2
3 and 4
explanation: The project log brings together records: daily log, lessons log, issue register, risk register, quality register and product register. The business case is a baseline, not a record in the project log, and the work package description is a separate management product by which the PM hands work over to the team.

image.alt: Two containers: the PID with nine management approaches and the project log with six records, from the daily log to the product register.

question: Fill in the missing word: PRINCE2 divides management products into three types – baselines, records and ______.
options: reports
registers
plans
approaches
explanation: Management products are either baselines (approved and subsequently change-controlled, e.g. the business case, plans, the PID), records (dynamic records, e.g. the contents of the project log), or reports (reports capturing status at a point in time, e.g. a highlight report or end stage report). Registers, plans and approaches fall into these types; they are not a separate type.

question: Which of the following management products is a baseline, i.e. is subject to change control once approved?
options: Business case
Highlight report
Risk register
Daily log
explanation: Once approved, the business case becomes part of the baseline and changes only in a controlled way (it is updated mainly at stage boundaries). A highlight report is a report capturing status at a given date, and the risk register and daily log are records that are continuously added to without change control.

image.alt: Two containers: the PID with nine management approaches and the project log with six records, from the daily log to the product register.

question: What replaced the configuration item records and product status account from the 6th edition in PRINCE2 7?
options: The product register as part of the project log
The quality register as part of the project log
The product breakdown structure in the project plan
The configuration management approach in the PID
explanation: In the 7th edition, the products that the project is to deliver, including their status and acceptance, are tracked in the product register stored in the project log; it replaced both the configuration item records and the product status account. The quality register, by contrast, records planned and performed quality control activities. A configuration management approach is not among the approaches in the 7th edition PID.

image.alt: Two containers: the PID with nine management approaches and the project log with six records, from the daily log to the product register.

question: Which of the following approaches is NOT part of the PID in PRINCE2 7?
options: Change control approach
Digital and data management approach
Sustainability management approach
Commercial management approach
explanation: The PID in PRINCE2 7 contains nine approaches: benefits, change (organisational change), commercial, communication, digital and data, issue, quality, risk and sustainability management approach. Change control approach is the name from the 6th edition – control of changes to the baseline is now described by the issue management approach.

image.alt: Two containers: the PID with nine management approaches and the project log with six records, from the daily log to the product register.

question: Which statement about the benefits management approach in PRINCE2 7 is correct?
options: It is part of the PID, where it is listed alongside the other approaches
It is a separate product outside the PID, owned by the business layer
It is a chapter of the project brief and is not updated after initiation
It is part of the end project report and is created only when the project is closed
explanation: In PRINCE2 7, the benefits management approach is one of the nine approaches in the PID; in the 6th edition it was a separate product outside the PID. It is created during initiation, reviewed at stage boundaries and, when the project is closed, updated with the plan for post-project benefits reviews.

image.alt: Two containers: the PID with nine management approaches and the project log with six records, from the daily log to the product register.

question: What is true of the project brief after initiation is completed?
options: It is replaced by the PID and is no longer updated
It is updated at every stage boundary as a baseline
It becomes part of the project log as one of its records
It is handed over to the business layer as a report on the outcome of initiation
explanation: The project brief is created in the Starting up a project process as the basis for the decision to start initiation. During initiation its content is elaborated into the PID, which replaces it, and the brief is then no longer maintained. The baseline that is reviewed at stage boundaries is the PID.

question: What is the purpose of the Business case practice?
options: To make it possible to judge whether the project is desirable, viable and achievable, and to support investment decision-making
To define and establish the project's accountability structure, i.e. to determine who is responsible in the project for what and to whom
To monitor and compare actual results against the plan and forecast whether the project will achieve its objectives on time
To collect and evaluate issues and keep all changes to the project baseline under proper control
explanation: The Business case practice answers the question "why": it provides mechanisms to judge whether the project is (and remains) desirable, viable and achievable, and thereby supports decision-making on starting and continuing the investment. The accountability structure is the purpose of the Organizing practice, comparing actuals with the plan the purpose of the Progress practice, and control of changes to the baseline the purpose of the Issues practice.

question: Fill in the missing word: A tangible or intangible specialist product that results from project activity is referred to in the Business case practice as an ______.
options: output
outcome
benefit
capability
explanation: An output is a specialist product that the project delivers – for example a new information system or a user manual. An outcome is the result of a change, i.e. changed behaviour or circumstances, a benefit is a measurable improvement arising from an outcome, and a capability is a complete set of outputs needed to achieve an outcome.

image.alt: A chain of outputs, capabilities, outcomes, benefits and business objectives, with a definition and an example for each link.

question: What does the term capability denote in the Business case practice?
options: A complete set of outputs that is needed to achieve an outcome
A measurable improvement that the investing organisation perceives as an advantage
The skills and experience of the team needed to create the project's outputs
A change in behaviour or circumstances brought about by the use of the outputs in practice
explanation: In PRINCE2 7, a capability is a complete set of outputs that makes it possible to achieve an outcome: the outputs form a capability, which is put into operation and the outcome arises. A measurable improvement is a benefit and a change in behaviour or circumstances is an outcome. Team skills (team capability) are a different concept, belonging to the People element.

image.alt: A chain of outputs, capabilities, outcomes, benefits and business objectives, with a definition and an example for each link.

question: A hospital is introducing an electronic patient appointment booking system. Which of the following is an outcome?
options: Patients book appointments online and reception no longer handles telephone bookings
A deployed booking system including a mobile app and user documentation
A 15% annual reduction in patient booking costs compared with the situation before the project
The system, trained staff and new procedures ready for use together
explanation: An outcome is the result of a change – changed behaviour or circumstances, here the fact that patients actually book appointments online. The deployed system is an output, a complete set of outputs ready for use is a capability, and the measurable cost reduction is a benefit that follows from the outcome.

image.alt: A chain of outputs, capabilities, outcomes, benefits and business objectives, with a definition and an example for each link.

question: What is a dis-benefit according to PRINCE2 7?
options: A measurable deterioration resulting from an outcome, which some party perceives as negative
The risk that one of the project's planned benefits will not be achieved in full or on time
A project cost that exceeds the amount approved in the business case by more than the tolerance
A benefit that appears only after the project is closed and which the board therefore cannot verify in any way
explanation: A dis-benefit is a measurable negative consequence of an outcome that some stakeholder perceives as a deterioration – for example longer waiting times for a certain group of clients. Unlike a risk, it is an expected consequence, not an uncertain event. Neither a cost overrun nor a deferred benefit is a dis-benefit.

image.alt: A chain of outputs, capabilities, outcomes, benefits and business objectives, with a definition and an example for each link.

question: Which sequence correctly captures the chain through which a project contributes to the organisation's strategy?
options: Outputs → capabilities → outcomes → benefits → business objectives
Outputs → outcomes → capabilities → benefits → business objectives
Capabilities → outputs → outcomes → business objectives → benefits
Outcomes → outputs → capabilities → benefits → business objectives
explanation: Outputs are assembled into capabilities; putting them into operation produces outcomes, which are measured by benefits and dis-benefits, and these lead to business objectives. A capability therefore lies between outputs and outcomes – the 6th edition knew only the shortened chain outputs → outcomes → benefits.

image.alt: A chain of outputs, capabilities, outcomes, benefits and business objectives, with a definition and an example for each link.

question: Fill in the missing word: The owner of the business case in PRINCE2 7 is the ______.
options: executive
project manager
senior user
business layer
explanation: The owner of the business case is the executive, who is the single point of accountability for the project and is responsible for securing funding and for the ongoing justification of the project. The project manager may prepare and update the content of the business case but is not its owner; the senior user is responsible for specifying and realising benefits, and the business layer commissions the project.

question: Which role is responsible for specifying the benefits and for demonstrating that the expected benefits are actually being realised?
options: Senior user
Executive
Senior supplier
Project manager
explanation: The senior user represents those who will use the outputs and realise benefits through them; this is why they specify the benefits and are responsible for demonstrating that the expected benefits are on track and being realised. The executive owns the business case as a whole and is responsible for the ongoing justification of the project, but does not specify the users' benefits.

question:
Which two of the following statements about the development of the business case are true?
1. The outline business case is created in the Starting up a project process.
2. The full business case is created in the Controlling a stage process.
3. The business case is updated in the Managing a stage boundary process.
4. After the project is authorised, the business case no longer changes.
options: 1 and 3
1 and 2
2 and 4
3 and 4
explanation: The outline business case is prepared during Starting up a project, the full business case during Initiating a project, and at each stage boundary (Managing a stage boundary) the business case is updated. After the project is authorised it is therefore still maintained so that the board can verify the ongoing justification of the project.

question: Which steps make up the business case management technique in PRINCE2 7?
options: Develop, check, maintain, confirm benefits
Develop, verify, maintain, confirm benefits
Identify, assess, plan, implement, communicate
Capture, assess, recommend, decide, implement
explanation: The business case management technique in PRINCE2 7 has the steps develop, check, maintain and confirm benefits. The step "verify" comes from the 6th edition; Identify–Assess–Plan–Implement–Communicate is the risk management technique and Capture–Assess–Recommend–Decide–Implement is the issue management technique.

question: When does the project board check the business case according to the business case management technique?
options: At every decision point – when authorising initiation, the project and each subsequent stage
Only once, when authorising the project, when it assesses the full business case contained in the PID
Only when the project is closed, when it compares actual costs and benefits with the planned ones
Only at the request of the senior user, who is responsible for specifying and realising the project's benefits
explanation: The board checks the business case at every decision point: the outline business case when authorising initiation, the full business case when authorising the project and the updated business case when authorising each subsequent stage. A one-off check, or a check only at the end, would not make it possible to ensure the ongoing justification of the project.

question: When, according to PRINCE2 7, are the project's benefits confirmed?
options: During later stages, if benefits appear already during the project, and above all after its closure
Exclusively when the project is closed, when the PM includes them in the end project report and lessons report
Only at stage boundaries, when the project manager updates the business case and the project plan
Before the project is authorised, so that the board can verify that the benefits stated in the business case are realistic
explanation: Benefits are confirmed as soon as they can be measured: some already during later stages of the project, but most only after it ends, when the outputs are used in day-to-day operations. Post-project reviews lie outside the project lifecycle and are planned in the benefits management approach. When the project is authorised, benefits are only forecast, so they cannot yet be confirmed.

question: What does the PID: benefits management approach describe?
options: Who will measure benefits, how and when, and which benefits reviews will take place even after the project ends
The calculation of return on investment and a comparison of solution options from which the board chooses the best one
The way in which the project will support people in moving from the current to the target state
A list of all products the project will deliver, including their current status and date of acceptance
explanation: The benefits management approach describes the steps that ensure outcomes are achieved and benefits confirmed: what will be measured, who will carry out the measurement and when, baseline values, and the plan of benefits reviews, including those after the project ends. Comparing options and return on investment belong in the business case, supporting people's transition belongs in the change management approach, and the list of products in the product register.

question: What is the PID: sustainability management approach used for?
options: It describes the activities, reviews and checks that will ensure the project's sustainability targets are met
It describes how the project's data and digital tools will be obtained, stored and secured
It sets out how suppliers will be selected and how the contractual relationship with them will be managed
It determines how, after the project ends, it will be verified that its products actually delivered the expected benefits
explanation: The sustainability management approach describes the steps, reviews and checks that ensure the project meets its performance targets for sustainability (sustainability is one of the seven performance targets). Work with data and digital tools is addressed by the digital and data management approach, relationships with suppliers by the commercial management approach, and verification of benefits by the benefits management approach.

question: On what basis should the preferred solution option be chosen in the business case?
options: It should keep all seven performance targets within tolerances, even if it is not the cheapest
It should have the lowest costs, because costs limit the organisation's investment risk the most
It should have the shortest delivery time, so that benefits arrive as soon as possible after the start
It should promise the highest benefits; costs and risks are assessed only in the project plan
explanation: PRINCE2 7 stresses that the preferred option should balance all seven performance targets (including sustainability) within tolerances; the cheapest or fastest option is not necessarily the best. Choosing on a single criterion ignores the balance between benefits, costs and risks on which the business case rests.

question: What is the purpose of the Organizing practice?
options: To define and establish the project's accountability structure – who is responsible for what and accountable to whom
To judge whether the project is desirable, viable and achievable, and to support the investment decision
To ensure that the organisation and its people successfully move from the current to the required target state
To facilitate communication and control by defining the products and the means by which they will be delivered
explanation: The Organizing practice answers the question "who": it defines and establishes the project's accountability structure – the roles, their responsibilities and the relationships between them. Judging desirability and viability is the purpose of the Business case practice, the transition to the target state is the domain of change management (the People element), and defining products and the means of delivering them belongs to the Plans practice.

question: Which three interests must be represented on the project board according to PRINCE2 7?
options: Business, user and supplier
Business, user and project manager
Customer, supplier and regulator
Sponsor, user and project office
explanation: A project must balance three interests: business (whether the investment makes sense – represented by the executive), user (those who will use the products and realise the benefits – the senior user) and supplier (those who provide resources and expertise – the senior supplier). The project manager is not a board member, and a regulator is a stakeholder, not one of the three interests.

image.alt: PRINCE2 7 organisation chart: the business layer, the Project Board with three roles, the Project manager and the Team manager with the project assurance, change authority and project support roles.

question: Fill in the missing word: The level that stands outside the project management team, commissions the project, provides the project mandate and sets the project tolerance is called the ______ in PRINCE2 7.
options: business layer
project board
programme office
directing level
explanation: The business layer is the commissioning level outside the project management team: it provides the project mandate, appoints the executive and sets the project tolerances. The project board forms the directing level inside the project and directs the project within the tolerances the business layer has set for it. In the 6th edition this level was called corporate, programme management or customer.

image.alt: PRINCE2 7 organisation chart: the business layer, the Project Board with three roles, the Project manager and the Team manager with the project assurance, change authority and project support roles.

question: What is the difference between the project management team and the project team?
options: The project team includes everyone who works on the project; the PMT is made up of the project management roles
The PMT includes everyone who works on the project; the project team is made up only of the project board and the PM
The project team is the team of a single supplier; the PMT is the sum of all project teams
They are synonyms, which PRINCE2 7 uses depending on the size and complexity of the particular project
explanation: The project management team is the structure of project management roles – the project board, the project manager and, as needed, team managers, project assurance, project support and change authority. The project team is a broader term: it includes everyone who gives their time to the project, including members of the teams that create the products.

image.alt: PRINCE2 7 organisation chart: the business layer, the Project Board with three roles, the Project manager and the Team manager with the project assurance, change authority and project support roles.

question: How are decisions made on the project board according to PRINCE2?
options: The executive decides, supported and advised by the senior user and senior supplier
By voting – each of the three interests has one vote and a simple majority of members' votes decides
By consensus – no binding decision can be made without the agreement of all board members
The project manager decides as chair of the board on the basis of the other members' recommendations
explanation: The project board is not a democracy run by voting: the final decision belongs to the executive, who is the single point of accountability for the project, and the senior user and senior supplier provide support and advice for their areas. The project manager is not a board member – he presents information and recommendations to the board.

question:
Which two of the following statements about the executive role are true?
1. There is always exactly one executive in a project.
2. The executive is responsible for securing the project's funding.
3. In a small project, the executive may also hold the project manager role.
4. The executive is elected by the members of the project board.
options: 1 and 2
3 and 4
1 and 3
2 and 4
explanation: The executive is the single point of accountability for the project, which is why there is always exactly one in a project; the executive owns the business case and secures funding. The executive role cannot be combined with the project manager role even in a small project. The executive is not elected by the board – the business layer appoints them.

question: What is the senior user responsible for?
options: For how user requirements are captured and for the users' acceptance of the products
For the quality of the products delivered by suppliers and for the technical integrity of the entire solution
For owning the business case, securing funding and the ongoing justification of the project
For day-to-day management of the project within the tolerances set by the project board
explanation: The senior user represents those who will use, operate or maintain the products: they are responsible for how user requirements are captured, monitor whether the products meet those requirements, and ensure the products are handed over to and accepted by users. The quality of supplier products is the responsibility of the senior supplier, the business case is owned by the executive, and day-to-day management is the PM's task.

question: Which role provides the resources for creating the project's products and is responsible for their quality and for the technical integrity of the solution?
options: Senior supplier
Senior user
Project assurance
Executive
explanation: The senior supplier represents the interests of suppliers: they provide the suppliers' resources and people and are responsible for the quality of the products the suppliers deliver and for the technical integrity of the solution. The senior user represents users and their requirements, the executive the business interest, and project assurance merely independently verifies that the project is being managed properly.

question: Who must NOT perform project assurance?
options: The project manager who manages the project
An internal auditor appointed for the project by the executive
A representative of users appointed by the senior user
An external expert hired by the senior supplier
explanation: Project assurance must be independent of the project manager – so it must not be performed by the PM, a team manager or project support. Board members are responsible for the assurance of their own areas and may delegate it to other persons, for example an internal auditor (business assurance), a user representative (user assurance) or a technical expert (supplier assurance).

image.alt: PRINCE2 7 organisation chart: the business layer, the Project Board with three roles, the Project manager and the Team manager with the project assurance, change authority and project support roles.

question: Who is responsible for project assurance in a PRINCE2 project?
options: The members of the project board, each for the area of interest they represent
The project manager, who may use project support or the PMO for this
The quality assurance department of the whole organisation
The change authority, which assesses all proposed changes in the project
explanation: Project assurance is the responsibility of the project board members – the executive for business assurance, the senior user for user assurance and the senior supplier for supplier assurance; they may perform it themselves or delegate it to other persons. Quality assurance is an independent function of the organisation outside the project, whereas project assurance serves the board. Neither the PM nor project support may perform assurance.

image.alt: PRINCE2 7 organisation chart: the business layer, the Project Board with three roles, the Project manager and the Team manager with the project assurance, change authority and project support roles.

question: Fill in the missing word: If the authority to decide on requests for change and off-specifications has not been delegated to anyone, the role of change authority is performed by the ______.
options: project board
project manager
senior user
business layer
explanation: The change authority is a person or group to whom the board delegates decision-making on requests for change and off-specifications within set limits and with a change budget. If the board does not delegate this authority, the change authority is the project board itself. The project manager can be the change authority only if the board expressly entrusts it to them.

image.alt: PRINCE2 7 organisation chart: the business layer, the Project Board with three roles, the Project manager and the Team manager with the project assurance, change authority and project support roles.

question: Which statement about the team manager role is correct?
options: It is optional; if nobody holds it, the project manager manages the team members directly
It is mandatory; every work package must be taken over by an appointed team manager
The team manager submits checkpoint reports directly to the project board and the executive
The team manager sets the stage tolerance within which the project manager works
explanation: The team manager role is optional – in smaller projects it can be held by the PM, who then manages team members directly. The team manager takes over work packages from the PM, delivers their products within the agreed tolerances and submits checkpoint reports to the project manager, not to the board. The stage tolerance is set by the project board.

image.alt: PRINCE2 7 organisation chart: the business layer, the Project Board with three roles, the Project manager and the Team manager with the project assurance, change authority and project support roles.

question: Who is responsible for project support if nobody has been appointed to this role?
options: Project manager
Executive
Project assurance
Team manager
explanation: Project support (administration, planning support, maintaining registers and tools) is the responsibility of the project manager; the PM may delegate it, for example, to a project office (PMO). Project support must be kept separate from project assurance so that independent verification is preserved.

image.alt: PRINCE2 7 organisation chart: the business layer, the Project Board with three roles, the Project manager and the Team manager with the project assurance, change authority and project support roles.

question:
Which two of the following statements about setting tolerances are true?
1. The project tolerance is set by the business layer.
2. The stage tolerance is set by the project manager.
3. The stage tolerance is set by the project board.
4. The work package tolerance is set by the team manager.
options: 1 and 3
1 and 2
2 and 4
3 and 4
explanation: Tolerances are delegated from the top down: the business layer sets the project tolerance, the project board the stage tolerance and the project manager the work package tolerance (in the work package description). The team manager may then set tolerances for members of their team, but does not determine the work package tolerance.

image.alt: A chain of the business layer, the Project Board, the Project manager and the Team manager: tolerances are set from the top down and exceptions are escalated from the bottom up.

question: What is a work breakdown structure (WBS) in PRINCE2 7?
options: A hierarchy of all the project's work that links the product breakdown to work packages
A hierarchical breakdown of all the products the project is to deliver, from the project product to sub-products
A diagram showing the order in which the project's products are created and the dependencies between them
A diagram of the project management team's roles with the lines of delegation of authority and reporting between levels
explanation: In PRINCE2 7 the WBS is newly part of the Organizing practice: it is a hierarchy of all the project's work that links the breakdown of products (the product breakdown structure) to work packages. The hierarchical breakdown of products is the product breakdown structure, the order and dependencies of products are shown by the product flow diagram, and the diagram of roles is the project management team structure.

question: What does the organizational design and development technique start with?
options: Understanding the organisational ecosystem in which the project will operate
Appointing the executive, who then appoints the project manager
Designing the organisational structure of the project management team and the reporting lines
Writing role descriptions for all members of the project board and team
explanation: The organizational design and development technique has five steps: understand the organisational ecosystem, design the project ecosystem, develop it, manage its changes and finally transition the project into the organisational ecosystem. Designing the team structure and role descriptions come into play only after understanding the environment in which the project will operate.

question: Which approach in the PID describes how the project will manage relationships with external suppliers that are governed by contracts?
options: Commercial management approach
Communication management approach
Issue management approach
Benefits management approach
explanation: The commercial management approach belongs to the Organizing practice and describes how the project manages commercial (contractual) relationships with suppliers. The communication management approach addresses communication with the project ecosystem, the issue management approach the management of issues and changes, and the benefits management approach the measurement and confirmation of benefits.

question: Which combination of roles does PRINCE2 7 permit?
options: The project manager also holds the team manager role
The executive also holds the project manager role
The project manager also performs project assurance
The project has two executives with shared accountability
explanation: In smaller projects the project manager may also hold the team manager or project support role. The executive must not also be the project manager, and there is always only one executive in a project. Project assurance must be independent of the project manager, so the PM must not perform it.

question: What is the purpose of the Plans practice in PRINCE2 7?
options: To facilitate communication and control by defining the products and how, when, by whom and at what cost they will be delivered
To provide mechanisms to judge whether the project is desirable, viable and achievable and whether it remains so
To compare actual and planned progress, forecast the development of the project's objectives and manage deviations leading to an exception
To define and establish the project's accountability structure, i.e. who is responsible for what in the project and accountable to whom
explanation: The Plans practice facilitates communication and control: it defines the products (what) and the means of delivering them (who, how, where, an estimate of when and at what cost) so that the business case (why) is fulfilled. Judging desirability, viability and achievability is the purpose of the Business case practice, comparing actuals with the plan and managing deviations that of the Progress practice, and the accountability structure that of the Organizing practice.

question: Who prepares the initiation stage plan, and in which process?
options: The project manager in the Starting up a project process
The project manager in the Initiating a project process, together with the project plan
The Project Board in the Directing a project process when authorising initiation
The project manager in the Managing a stage boundary process at the end of SU
explanation: The initiation stage plan is prepared by the project manager already in Starting up a project, and the Project Board approves it together with the project brief when authorising initiation (Directing a project). The project plan is created only in Initiating a project, and Managing a stage boundary is first used only at the end of the initiation stage – SU is not a stage.

question: Which statement about team plans corresponds to PRINCE2 7?
options: They are optional and are prepared by the team manager to carry out an assigned work package
They are mandatory for every work package and are approved by the Project Board when authorising a stage
They are prepared by the project manager in the Managing a stage boundary process for each team
They replace the stage plan if the stage is carried out by an external supplier with its own methodology
explanation: A team plan is optional; it is prepared by the team manager (typically when accepting a work package in Managing product delivery) and agreed with the project manager.
