question: Which of the following is an objective of the Managing product delivery process?
options: To ensure that the work allocated to the team is authorised and agreed
To ensure that the business case is updated at the end of each stage
To ensure that the board explicitly decides to start project initiation
To ensure that open issues are passed into follow-on action recommendations
explanation: The objectives of Managing product delivery include that the work allocated to the team is authorised and agreed, that team managers know what they are to deliver and with what effort, cost and dates, that products meet quality expectations within tolerance and that the PM receives accurate information about progress. Updating the business case belongs to Managing a stage boundary, the decision on initiation to Directing a project and follow-on action recommendations to Closing a project.

question: What is, according to PRINCE2 7, one of the objectives of the Controlling a stage process?
options: To focus on delivering the stage's products and to prevent uncontrolled change
To select the project approach and prepare the project brief for the board's decision
To confirm acceptance of the project product and pass on open risks
To set the project tolerances and appoint the executive on behalf of the business layer
explanation: The objectives of Controlling a stage include keeping attention on delivering the stage's products and avoiding uncontrolled change (a departure from the agreed products and delivery method), keeping risks and issues under control and continually reviewing the business case. Selecting the project approach belongs to Starting up a project, confirming acceptance to Closing a project and setting the project tolerances to the business layer.

question: What is the purpose of the Managing a stage boundary process?
options: To give the board the basis for assessing the stage, approving the next stage and confirming the justification
To enable the PM to assign work to teams and keep the stage within tolerance through corrective actions
To confirm acceptance of the project product and recognise that the project's objectives have been achieved
To verify before initiation whether we have a viable and worthwhile project and to prepare the project brief
explanation: Managing a stage boundary enables the project manager to give the Project Board enough information to assess the success of the current stage, approve the next stage plan, review the updated project plan and confirm the continuing justification of the project and the acceptability of the risks. Assigning work is Controlling a stage, confirming acceptance is Closing a project and verification before initiation is Starting up a project.

question:
Which two of the following statements about the Managing a stage boundary process are true?
1. It is used by the Project Board to authorise the next stage.
2. It is used for the first time at the end of the initiation stage.
3. It is used only once, at the end of the initiation stage.
4. It is used whenever the Project Board requests an exception plan.
options: 2 and 4
1 and 2
1 and 3
3 and 4
explanation: Managing a stage boundary is the project manager's process: it is used for the first time at the end of the initiation stage, then at the end of each subsequent stage except the last, and in addition whenever (even during the last stage) the board requests an exception plan. The next stage is authorised by the Project Board in its Directing a project process.

question: Fill in the missing word: In the process of managing a stage boundary, the project manager evaluates the stage that is ending and prepares an ______ for the Project Board.
options: end stage report
end project report
highlight report
checkpoint report
explanation: When evaluating a stage in Managing a stage boundary, the PM prepares an end stage report – an overview of the stage's performance, the status of the business case and risks, and the basis for the request for the next stage; possibly also a lessons report. The end project report is created in Closing a project, the highlight report is a regular report during a stage and the checkpoint report is sent by the team manager to the project manager.

question: What is the purpose of the Closing a project process?
options: To confirm acceptance of the project product and recognise that the project's objectives have been achieved
To give the board the basis for assessing the stage and approving the next stage plan
To evaluate all the benefits, because after closure their realisation is no longer measured
To enable the Project Board to take over from the PM the day-to-day management of the final delivery stage
explanation: Closing a project provides a fixed point at which acceptance of the project product is confirmed and it is recognised that the project's objectives (or their approved changes) have been achieved; in the case of premature closure it ensures proper closure. The basis for approving the next stage is provided by Managing a stage boundary, many benefits are measured only after the project and the board does not take over day-to-day management.

question: What triggers the Closing a project process?
options: The end of the project is approaching, or the board requests premature closure
Exclusively approval of the last end stage report in the Directing a project process
The result of a benefits review after the project ends
A team manager's request to finish the last work package in Managing product delivery
explanation: Closing a project is triggered either by the approaching end of the project (project end approaching) from Controlling a stage in the last stage, or by the board's request for premature closure (premature close) from Directing a project. At the end of the last stage no end stage report is prepared, post-project benefits reviews take place only after closure and the team manager does not trigger project closure.

question: How are issues and risks that remain open handled when the project is closed?
options: They are passed on in the form of follow-on action recommendations
All of them must be resolved, otherwise the project cannot be closed
They are transferred to the lessons report as lessons for other projects
They remain in the issue register, which the business layer takes over as a baseline
explanation: Open issues and risks are passed, at closure, to those who will be responsible for the products after the project, in the form of follow-on action recommendations. The project need not stay open because of them; the lessons report captures lessons, not unresolved tasks, and the registers in the project log are records, not baselines.

question: Which of the following activities does NOT belong to the Closing a project process?
options: Preparing the next stage plan and updating the project plan
Verifying that users have accepted the project product
Assessing the benefits achieved so far and updating the benefits management approach
Reviewing the project's performance against its baselines
explanation: In Closing a project the acceptance of the project product is verified, the project's performance is reviewed against its baselines, the benefits achieved so far are assessed and the benefits management approach is updated with post-project reviews. Preparing the next stage plan and updating the project plan belong to Managing a stage boundary, which is not used at the end of the last stage.
